nodes.name: Lemma 8
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $G$ is $i$-homogenous and has no positive cycles and no sources. Let $f$ be an and-or-net on $G$, let $x$ be a configuration on $V$, and let $r$ be the maximum length of a canalizing word from $(i,x_i)$. There is a word $w$, which does not contain $i$, such that $f^w(x)$ is an $i$-unstable configuration in $G$ and 
\[
|w|< F(n-r+1)+r-1.
\]
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 7
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $G$ is $i$-homogenous and has no positive cycles and no sources. Suppose also that $G$ has a positive path $P$ from a vertex $j$ to $i$ such that $j$ is of in-degree at least two, and all the vertices of $P$ distinct from $j$ are of in-degree one (if $i$ is of in-degree at least two, this path always exists and is the trivial graph whose unique vertex is $i$). Let $f$ be the and-net on $G$ and let $x,y$ be configurations on $V$. There is a word $w$ such that $f^w(x)_i=f^w(y)_i=0$ and 
\[
|w|< 2F(n+2).
\]
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 9
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $G$ is homogenous and has no positive cycles, no sources and no initial cycles. Let $f$ be the and-net on $G$. For every configurations $x,y$ on $V$, there is a word $w$ such that $f^w(x)=f^w(y)$ and 
\[
|w|\leq 3F(n+4)-3.
\]
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 3
nodes.statement: If $G$ is homogenous, then every switch of $G$ is homogenous.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 2
nodes.statement: If $G$ has an initial cycle, then no BN on $G$ is synchronizing.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 6
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be a BN on $G$, $i\in V$ and $a\in\{0,1\}$. Let $w$ be a canalizing word from $(i,a)$ with image $b$, and suppose that no sources of $G$ are in $\{w\}$. For every $j\in\{w\}$, $G$ has a path from $i$ to $j$, whose internal vertices are in $\{w\}$, which is positive if $a=b_j$ and negative otherwise.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 5
nodes.statement:
Suppose that $G$ is $i$-homogenous and has no positive cycles and no sources. Let $f$ be an and-or-net on $G$. Let $x$ be a configuration on $V$ and let $v$ be a longest canalizing word from $(i,x_i)$. There is a word $w$ such that $f^w(x)_i\neq x_i$~and
\[
|w|< F(n-|v|+2)+|v|.
\]
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 11
nodes.statement: Suppose that $G$ is homogenous and has no positive cycles, no sources and no initial cycles. The and-net on $G$ has a synchronizing word of length at most $10(\sqrt{5}+1)^n$.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: thm:main2
nodes.statement: Suppose that $G$ is homogenous and has no positive cycles, no sources and no initial cycles. Then every and-or-net on $G$ has a synchronizing word of length at most $10(\sqrt{5}+1)^n$.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: thm:main
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a non-trivial strongly connected signed digraph on $[n]$ without positive~cycles, and let $f$ be a BN on $G$. For all $i\in [n]$ and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, we have $f^w(x)_i\neq x_i$ for some word~$w$.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 10
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be a BN with component set $V$ and suppose that, for every configurations $x,y$ on $V$, there is a word $u$ such that $f^u(x)=f^u(y)$ and $|u|\leq k$. For every non-empty subset $X\subseteq \{0,1\}^V$, there is a word $w$ such that $|f^w(X)|=1$ and $|w|\leq k(|X|-1)$. Taking $X=\{0,1\}^V$, we deduce that $f$ has a synchronizing word of length at most $k(2^n-1)$.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: thm:chromatic
nodes.statement: Suppose that $G$ has no positive cycles and no loops. There are disjoint subsets $I,J\subseteq V$ with $I\cup J=V$ such that $G[I]$ and $G[J]$ are acyclic.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: thm:fast
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a strongly connected signed digraph on $[n]$ without positive cycles, which is not a cycle. At least one and-or-net on $G$ has a synchronizing word of length at most $5n(\sqrt{2})^n$.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: thm:every_synch
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 12
nodes.statement: Suppose that $G$ is simple and has a spanning full-positive out-tree $T$, where the root $r$ has only negative in-neighbors and is of in-degree at least two. Suppose also that $G$ has no full-positive cycle, and that each positive cycle containing $r$ has at least four negative arcs. Let $f$ be the and-net on $G$. For every configurations $x,y$ on $V$ there is a word $w$ such that $f^w(x)=f^w(y)$ and $|w|\leq 5n$. Furthermore, if $r$ has a loop, then $f$ has a synchronizing word of length at most $7n$.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 13
nodes.statement: Suppose that $G$ is strong, has no positive cycles, and is not a cycle. There is an and-or-net $f$ on $G$ such that the following holds. For every configurations $x,y$ on $V$, there is a word $w$ such that $f^w(x)=f^w(y)$ and $|w|\leq 5n$. Furthermore, if $G$ has a loop, then $f$ has a synchronizing word of length at most $7n$.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: Lemma 14
nodes.statement: Let $I\subseteq V$ such that $G\setminus I$ is acyclic, and let $w$ be a topological sort of $G\setminus I$. Let $f$ be a BN on $G$. For every configurations $x,y$ on $V$ with $x_I=y_I$ we have $f^w(x)=f^w(y)$.
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: thm:fixed_point
nodes.statement:
The following conditions are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\psi$ is not satisfiable. 
\item Every BN on $G_\psi$ has at most one fixed point.
\item There is a word of length $12n+12m+11$ which synchronizes every BN on~$G_\psi$.
\item Every BN on $G_\psi$ is synchronizing.
\end{enumerate}
nodes.section: Figure 2: Dependency graph of the main and auxiliary results.

nodes.name: thm:complexity
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a signed digraph on $[n]$. If $G$ is not strongly connected or has a positive cycle, then it is coNP-hard to decide if every and-or-net on $G$ is synchronizing (even if $G$ has maximum in-degree at most $2$ and a vertex meeting every cycle).
